submitter: bugs_open/297 — bugfix_297_tool_recreation_context lane. Filed 2026-08-17 by the bugfix_275_silent_row_caps lane as a ticket from its own census; unowned (who-owns.py names only the filing commit, and a grep of ~25 live session transcripts — the only instrument that sees uncommitted work — shows no session on it).
rationale:
SCOPE NOTE FIRST, because this submission is FORCED past the client-side filter and a reviewer deserves to know why. The 2026-07-17 ruling scopes this gate to platform/, internal/, pkg/ so that docs and site content never spend council credits. This change is NEITHER: it is a config-only migration that rewrites a LIVE agent's SQL step in agent_definitions, which is live on apply, needs no roll, and has no image-based rollback. The precedent is bugs_open/275's round on this exact mechanism, where the sharpest objection of the round (bug_historian: an unmarked column truncation) was against the MIGRATION half, not the Go half — so a config migration to a shared agent is precisely the shape this gate has already proved it catches things in. FORCE=1 with the reason stated, not silently.

THE DEFECT. tool-recreation-handler's `load_related_context` step ends `ORDER BY p.nav_order LIMIT 10`. Those rows become the 'Other Pages on This Site (for context)' block of the `analyze_tool` prompt — the input to the model that decides how a recreated interactive tool fits the site it lives on. MEASURED 2026-08-17 against live clients_db, with the query's own predicate (all pages of the site bar the subject): 25 sites, 19 of them hold MORE pages than the cap, median population 26, worst 107 (webdesign.co.uk, 108 pages). So at the median site the model sees 10 of 26 (38%) and at the worst 10 of 107 (9%). It is a SILENT cap: an LLM produces a plausible specification whether it saw 10 related pages or 107, so there is no wrong output to notice and no error to catch — bugs_open/275's mechanism exactly, register LCO-009. And the cut is by `nav_order`, so what survives is whatever sits highest in the NAVIGATION MENU, which is a judgement about menus and not about what a tool needs to know.

IT IS LIVE, NOT LATENT: llm_call_log holds 290 calls for agent_type='tool-recreation-handler' (most recent 2026-08-11) and 4 site_work_items name it as handler_agent. (orchestration_states.owner_agent_type returns 0 for this agent and is the WRONG instrument — it does not carry the handler's name. Had I trusted it I would have called this dormant.)

THE MEASUREMENT INVERTED 275'S REMEDY, AND THAT IS THE MAIN THING I WANT REVIEWED. The bug file's candidate 1 says: measure which column dominates the payload, bound THAT, and drop the row cap — which for 275 meant left(description,200) plus, after the council's objection, an explicit […truncated] marker. I did the measurement and it says the opposite here: NOTHING NEEDS BOUNDING. (a) The prompt renders one short line per row — `- {{.name}} ({{.page_type}}): {{.title}}` — read from the live template, not assumed. (b) Column extremes across all 727 pages: name <= 66 chars, title <= 144 (p99 ~114), page_type <= 16. (c) The whole-population rendered block at the WORST site is 8,810 chars (~2.2k tokens) against 735 today; at the median site ~2.2k chars — and it joins a prompt that already embeds the original page's ENTIRE raw HTML, typically tens of KB. So the honest fix is to delete the cap and truncate nothing. No marker is needed BECAUSE NOTHING IS TRUNCATED, and I am stating that explicitly so the absence of 446's marker machinery reads as a decision rather than an omission. Candidate 4 of the bug file ('do NOT just raise the number — 10 to 30 leaves 5 sites cut and re-creates this file in a month') is honoured: there is no number left to outgrow.

A SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT IN THE SAME QUERY, FOUND BY MEASURING RATHER THAN BY READING. `LEFT JOIN research_results rr ON rr.page_id = p.id AND rr.result_type = 'adoption_page'` has no one-row guarantee, and the table has no unique constraint on (page_id, result_type). One page ALREADY has two adoption_page rows — page 0747e2fc-43e1-4250-9f55-b1dbf5617482, the `index` page of site 00ff3af5, at nav_order 1 — so TODAY, on the live system, that site's prompt lists `index` twice inside the visible 10. I did not infer this; I ran the verbatim live query and counted the duplicate. Removing the cap widens this door (a page with N research rows would contribute N lines to an unbounded result), so the same edit closes it with LEFT JOIN LATERAL (... ORDER BY r.created_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) ON true: newest summary per page, exactly one row per page. I am asking the council to judge whether that belongs in this change or in its own — my reasoning is that 'the step returns the site's page population, exactly' is one coherent task, and that shipping the cap removal WITHOUT the de-dup would be knowingly widening a live defect.

WHY THE INNER LIMIT 1 IS NOT A NEW SILENT CAP. It is the fetch-one idiom, which LCO-009 excludes by design (n=1 is a lookup, not a truncation; 19 of the 26 live LIMITs are this shape and warning on them would train every reader to ignore the channel). And LCO-009's regex is END-ANCHORED, so a LIMIT inside a subquery is correctly ignored — a decision that 275's round-2 follow-up vindicated on two live cases (fix-proposer and visual-design-auditor put their LIMITs in subqueries and aggregate to one row). Both properties are stated rather than assumed, and the post-state verify block asserts that no MULTI-row LIMIT survives while permitting exactly this one.

SHAPE COMPATIBILITY, CHECKED NOT ASSUMED. The output_field is `related_pages`, and the ONLY consumer is the `analyze_tool` step of this same workflow (verified in the live config: input_fields lists related_pages, and the template's range block is the sole reference). Every row keeps the same four keys — name, title, page_type, summary — so no consumer sees a structural difference. `rr.summary` is SELECTED AND NEVER RENDERED, and is nearly absent estate-wide (21 of 727 pages carry an adoption_page row at all, max length 48 chars). I am deliberately NOT dropping it: that is 275's `category` reasoning — removing a column a future consumer might read is scope creep with non-zero risk for a negligible saving — and keeping it is also what makes the row shape byte-compatible.

NO GO CHANGE, AND WHY. The framework half of this class already exists and is committed: QueryDatabaseAction warns when a result set exactly fills its own literal LIMIT (register LCO-009, commit eb137faed, mutation-tested by the 275 lane, inert until the next chassis roll). Adding a second mechanism for the same class would be duplication; this submission removes 297's instance, and with it the future warning noise for this step. Reuse checked before writing, which is the objection the reuse_agent seat gated bugs_open/257 on.

ORDERING: none claimed, and I could not hold it if I wanted to (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §2 — HEAD is shared and review here is after the fact by design). The migration is config-only and independent of any binary; the commit carries Council-Submitted:, not Council-Reviewed:.

ARCHITECTURE SCOPE, ANSWERED BEFORE IT IS ASKED. This adds no field, no key, no contract, no capability, and no new authority on a shared seam — it rewrites one agent's own query string. Under the 2026-07-29 §1 test ('does it change what the shared MECHANISM guarantees') query_database's guarantee is untouched; under 2026-08-02 §2 / RFC_010 there is no new authority to gate opt-in; under RFC_022 there is no new optional key, so the optional-key budget is unmoved.

VALIDATED READ-ONLY BEFORE THE FILE WAS WRITTEN, so the sketches below are not aspirational: the proposed query returns 107 rows on the worst site (= population, was 10) and 40 rows on the fan-out site (= population 40, duplicate gone).

plan.summary: bugs_open/297: tool-recreation-handler's load_related_context shows the analysing model 10 of up to 107 of a site's pages, cut by nav_order — a silent row cap feeding an LLM prompt (LCO-009's class), live at 19 of 25 sites. Migration 453 drops the cap outright: measured, nothing needs bounding (the whole population at the worst site renders as 8,810 chars, in a prompt already carrying the page's full raw HTML), so unlike its sibling 275 there is no column truncation and therefore no truncation marker. The same edit replaces the plain research_results LEFT JOIN — which has no one-row guarantee and ALREADY duplicates a page on one live site — with a LEFT JOIN LATERAL taking the newest adoption_page summary per page, so the result is exactly the site's page population. Config-only, live on apply, snapshot + type-count pre-state gate + DO/RAISE post-state verify, with a gated rollback sidecar written before the apply.

edits.rationale: The fix. Drops `LIMIT 10` with nothing bounded in its place (§ rationale: the measurement says nothing needs bounding — worst-site whole population is 8,810 rendered chars), keeps `ORDER BY p.nav_order` as a presentation order now that order no longer decides visibility, and replaces the plain LEFT JOIN with a LATERAL so each page contributes exactly one row (the fan-out is live today on site 00ff3af5). NULLS LAST because research_results.created_at is NULLABLE and a NULL sorts FIRST under plain DESC — 0 of 21 adoption_page rows are NULL today, so the guard costs nothing and makes the bad state unreachable rather than merely unlikely. SAFETY SHAPE, and the whole executable file is shown below rather than the interesting parts — that is 275's misstep 3/5 lesson, where two rounds were spent on objections to sketches of my own writing that had omitted the safety lines: (1) snapshot_agent FIRST; (2) pre-state gate by TYPE-COUNT, not by id — the gate 275's council asked for, because an id-scoped UPDATE against a shadowed sibling row silently no-ops while the verify blocks pass; (3) the gate also refuses unless the step still carries BOTH the LIMIT 10 and the plain join, so a concurrent change by another session aborts rather than being clobbered; (4) post-state verify in DO/RAISE, never bare SELECTs, because ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result and a SELECT-only verify cannot stop the COMMIT. The verify asserts no MULTI-row LIMIT survives (permitting the LATERAL's fetch-one LIMIT 1 by design), that the LATERAL is present, that nav_order ordering was not lost, and that both param bindings are untouched.

DB config is LIVE ON APPLY — there is no image roll to gate it and no redeploy that undoes it — so the rollback exists BEFORE the forward apply, not after something looks wrong. It carries the same two guards in reverse: exactly one live row for the type, and a refusal unless the row currently carries 453's LATERAL text, so re-running it cannot silently revert a LATER change another session made on this shared tree. It restores the pre-453 string byte-for-byte (plain join, LIMIT 10) and verifies that restore in a DO/RAISE block. Uppercase _ROLLBACK suffix so run-migrations.sh's SIDECAR_RE excludes it from --apply while still listing it.

grounded_in: bugs_open/297 (the ticket) — "The rows become the *related context* an LLM is given when recreating a tool. A row-count `LIMIT` feeding a prompt is **silent by construction**: the model produces a plausible tool whether it saw 10 related pages or 107, so there is no wrong output to notice and no error to catch. ... The cut is by `nav_order`, so what survives is 'whatever sits highest in the navigation', which is a judgement about menus, not about what a tool needs to know."

bugs_open/297 fix candidate 1 — "Bound the PAYLOAD, not the row count — the shape that worked for 275. Measure which column dominates ... bound that, and drop the row cap. ... Do the measurement first." MEASURED 2026-08-17 and it says NO column needs bounding here: the prompt renders `- {{.name}} ({{.page_type}}): {{.title}}`; across all 727 pages name <= 66 chars, title <= 144, page_type <= 16; the whole population at the WORST site renders as 8,810 chars against 735 today, inside a prompt that already embeds the page's full raw HTML.

bugs_open/297 fix candidate 4 — "Do NOT just raise the number. 10 -> 30 leaves 5 sites still cut and re-creates this file in a month, because the population grows and the constant does not. That is precisely how 275 arrived." This change leaves no constant to outgrow.

bugs_open/297 verification note — "If you bound a column instead of rows, MARK the truncation. 275's first fix cut descriptions silently and the council caught it — an unmarked cut is the same defect one level down." NOT APPLICABLE HERE AND STATED SO ON PURPOSE: no column is bounded, nothing is truncated, so there is nothing to mark. The absence of 446's marker machinery is a decision, not an omission.

MEASURED 2026-08-17 (live clients_db), the census re-run from scratch rather than copied from the ticket: 25 sites (24 at filing), 19 of them with a population exceeding the cap, median population 26, worst 107 (webdesign.co.uk, 108 pages). The verbatim live query against the worst site returns exactly 10 rows today.

MEASURED 2026-08-17 — the live step is unchanged and there is exactly ONE active definition row (id 8701375f-81f7-4d92-ba39-c85f8489dada, version 1), so this agent is not one of the duplicate-active-row types; the migration gates on the type-count anyway, because being right by luck is not the same as being guarded (bugs_open/275 round 1, debug_historian).

MEASURED 2026-08-17 — the fan-out is LIVE, not hypothetical: `SELECT page_id, COUNT(*) FROM research_results WHERE result_type='adoption_page' GROUP BY page_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` returns page 0747e2fc-43e1-4250-9f55-b1dbf5617482, which is the `index` page of site 00ff3af5 at nav_order 1 — inside today's visible 10, so that site's prompt lists `index` twice right now.

VALIDATED READ-ONLY 2026-08-17, before the migration file was written: the proposed query returns 107 rows on site 6b49db8e (= population, was 10) and 40 rows on the fan-out site 00ff3af5 (= population 40, duplicate gone).

MEASURED 2026-08-17 — the agent is live, not dormant: llm_call_log holds 290 calls for agent_type='tool-recreation-handler' (most recent 2026-08-11). `orchestration_states.owner_agent_type` returns 0 for it and is the WRONG instrument; trusting it would have made this ticket read as dormant.

bugs_open/275 lane NOTES, on why the inner LIMIT 1 is safe and why no second detector is needed — "Only FIVE of the 'seven' are whole-result caps. `fix-proposer.load_last_bundle` puts its `LIMIT 2` inside a subquery and `string_agg`s the result into ONE row ... My end-anchored regex ignores both — correctly, and flagging them would have been a false positive on a real config." The framework detector (LCO-009) is committed at eb137faed and rides the next chassis roll; this submission adds no second mechanism for the same class.
plan.risks: 1) THE CHANGE I MOST WANT CHALLENGED: dropping the cap with nothing in its place. My case is arithmetic (worst site = 8,810 rendered chars ~2.2k tokens, median ~2.2k chars, inside a prompt already carrying the original page's full raw HTML at typically tens of KB), but the analyze_tool step's ai_service.max_tokens is an OUTPUT cap and I have not measured the assembled input token count end to end — I have measured the block this step contributes. If a seat thinks the block should still be bounded, the honest bound is a page COUNT with an explicit '(+N more pages not shown)' line, not a silent LIMIT. 2) SCOPE: I have combined the cap removal with a join de-dup. They are separable, and a reviewer may reasonably say the de-dup belongs in its own change; my reasoning is that removing the cap widens the fan-out door (a page with N research rows would contribute N lines to an unbounded result), so shipping only half would knowingly worsen a live defect. 3) The LATERAL's ordering: created_at is NULLABLE on research_results and a NULL sorts FIRST under plain DESC, which would let an untimestamped row win the 'newest' tie and pin a page to it. I raised this as a question, measured it (0 of 21 adoption_page rows are NULL today; both rows on the one affected page carry timestamps), and CLOSED it with NULLS LAST rather than leaving it as a reviewer's opinion — it costs nothing and makes the bad state unreachable. Residual: nothing chooses between two rows sharing a timestamp, which is arbitrary-but-stable and not worth a tiebreaker column. 4) Performance: the lateral runs once per page (107 at the worst site) rather than one hash join; idx_research_page and idx_research_created exist, and this step runs a handful of times a day, but it is a change in plan shape and I have not EXPLAINed it under production load. 5) Config is LIVE ON APPLY — no roll gates it, no redeploy undoes it. Mitigated by the snapshot, the type-count pre-state gate, the concurrent-change refusal and the gated rollback sidecar, all written before the apply. 6) End-to-end confirmation in llm_call_log.prompt_rendered can only come from the next real recreation run (most recent was 2026-08-11); I am recording that as OWED rather than claiming it, and what I can and do assert now is the query-level disconfirming pair.
